name: baldurs
description: Fire every CF_PACK_BALDURS weapon ability and assert the governing criterion: classes playable, game does not break, everything fails safely. Magnitude is not the subject.
notes: WHY THIS PACK GETS ITS OWN SCENARIO: docs/research/test-checklist.md records a live NRE crash in the Chaos Mage abilities and flags CF_PACK_BALDURS as 'probably broken' by the same bug class -- GetCharacterAbilityRecord is dereferenced UNGUARDED at CharacterVisualHelper.cs:2567 and ~18 further sites, so a pack-authored ability id that resolves onto a body is a hard NRE crash in combat. This scenario is the check.

The four Baldur's classes and their display names, read from CF_PACK_BALDURS/classes.json -> LocKey -> localization/en.json: CF_WARLOCK_HEXBLADE = 'Hexblade Warlock', CF_BATTLEMASTER = 'Battle Master', CF_NECROMANCER = 'Necromancer', CF_SKELETON_WARRIOR = 'Skeleton Warrior'.

CF_PACK_BALDURS has NO statuses.json and its abilities.json is literally {}. Every ability the pack's items grant is a VANILLA ability id, and its one status reference is the vanilla STATUS_CURSE_00 (SKILL_CF_CURSED_STRIKES, Trigger ON_CRIT). So this scenario asserts on vanilla ids by design, not by oversight.

BALDUR'S CLASSES ARE NOT OUR FIVE. The identity tell here names a Baldur's class, and the Shepherd/Thief/Corsair/Bladedancer blocklist still applies -- those four are vanilla and would mean the fixture was built with set_class.

The pass/fail split that matters: '[ClassForge] Recipe effect failed (skipped, rest of plan continues)' is a PASS for fail-safety and a FAIL for correctness. Any NullReferenceException / KeyNotFoundException is a FAIL for fail-safety, which is the criterion that actually governs.

fixture.notes: BUILD RECIPE. New campaign -> CHARACTER CREATION for every slot. NEVER crucible_party_set_class: it rewrites ConfigName but not the display name, so the class is right in state and every screenshot shows a stale vanilla name -- that voided a whole verification run here. Save, copy the .ftk2 out of GameRuns\ into %USERPROFILE%\Backups\ftk2-fixtures under this name, then set status to 'built'. Slots: 1 = Hexblade Warlock, 2 = Battle Master, 3 = Necromancer, 4 = Skeleton Warrior. Each must be carrying its class Thing (CF_ITEM_PACT_BLADE, CF_ITEM_COMMANDERS_LONGSWORD, CF_ITEM_NECROTIC_STAFF, CF_ITEM_BONE_CLAWS) or its abilities will not be on the bar.

setup.why: godmode ON tops HP up every tick and masks every HP effect.

enemies.why: Grim Resurrection and Relentless are both ON_KILL, so the sweep needs something that dies

steps.label: HEXBLADE WARLOCK -- Pact Blade dark bolt; Hexblade Bargain trades HP for power at ON_ABILITY_USED

asserts.why: the party is still on the board -- combat did not abort

tells.expect: a party HUD card reading "Hexblade Warlock"
the tile grid and the action menu are BOTH still drawn. One absent 3D model takes the whole combat venue down through _clearTileRenderState, and the symptom is a missing UI, not a missing creature

steps.label: BATTLE MASTER -- Commander's Longsword push; Relentless is ON_KILL

tells.expect: a party HUD card reading "Battle Master"
the target's HP bar dropped and it may have been pushed to another tile

steps.label: NECROMANCER -- Necrotic Staff summon; Grim Resurrection is ON_KILL and is the riskiest effect in the pack

tells.expect: if anything was summoned, a BODY on the board AND a card in the ally HUD. A summon that exists only in state is the invisible-mechanic FAIL

steps.label: SKELETON WARRIOR -- Bone Claws basic attack

tells.expect: a party HUD card reading "Skeleton Warrior"
all four cards read Hexblade Warlock / Battle Master / Necromancer / Skeleton Warrior
the tile grid, the timeline and the action menu are all still on screen after every pack ability has been fired. That is what fail-safety looks like
